text: The studio had this smell, cedar and clean sweat, like rain hitting warm stone. The afternoon light came through the tall windows, these long amber panels, and you could see the dust moving really slow. The mats were in rows, muted colors, moss and clay, that dawn ocean grey. At the front the teacher just flowed through it, very calm, voice low, unhurried. And everyone just folded and unfolded. It was like a forest of arms going up. Then the wave of spines curling forward. And she was in the back corner, in this faded blue shirt. She was holding it a lot longer than everyone else. You could hear her breathing, very steady. Like a metronome. And when we finally went to savasana, the room felt like it exhaled. The traffic was out there, murmuring, but it was just the heater humming and the pulse in her wrists, very small, persistent. And she closed her eyes. And for a second she was not late, not tired, not alone. And the teacher rang the bell, just a note, and it dissolved. Like salt in water. And she stayed still. Just let the quiet hold her.
